... 113 ### GitHub Issues-only setup
... 114 
... 115 With `[tracker] kind = "github"`, issue lifecycle is projected as `open`/`done`,
... 116 and an existing `in-progress` label marks active open issues. This is a compatibility
... 117 convention, not a Project workflow or proof of delivery. Ordinary tracker operations
... 118 never create or recolor labels.
... 119 
... 120 Before using `status = "in-progress"`, an authorized repository owner must explicitly
... 121 review this convention and ensure the label exists in the target repository. For
... 122 example, after checking existing labels:
... 123 
... 124 ```sh
... 125 gh label list --repo OWNER/REPO
... 126 gh label create in-progress --repo OWNER/REPO
... 127 ```
... 128 
... 129 These are manual setup commands, not actions performed by `devsys_work_item`. Do not
... 130 force an existing label's settings. If an update fails, its original GitHub error is
... 131 returned; missing setup is only one possible cause (permissions or another edit may
... 132 have failed). Inspect the error, re-read the issue and repository setup, and retry
... 133 explicitly after resolving the cause. A failed edit does not trigger issue closure
... 134 or reopening; GitHub edits are not promised to be transactional. Repo-file tracking
... 135 requires no label setup. Project integration is not provided by this convention.

commitMessages:
docs(decisions): preserve push approval audit record

The push guard treated the latest Dependabot failure as a red trunk even though the CI/CD workflow for that commit was green. Preserve the user-approved one-command decision generated during delivery rather than discard its audit trail.

docs(decisions): retain follow-up delivery approval

Preserve the second one-command push approval generated while Dependabot reported a failed undici update alongside successful CI/CD. Keeping the generated record makes the delivery audit complete.

fix(tracker)!: require owner setup before workflow label use

Existing repositories must retain control over workflow setup rather than gaining labels as a side effect of an issue status update. Keep GitHub's original refusal visible and explain how an owner can set up a missing marker and retry; do not perform subsequent lifecycle changes after the failed edit.

Record the approved revision 0.2 adoption plan and architecture decisions so later increments extend optional primitives without imposing a universal project workflow.

BREAKING CHANGE: GitHub issue updates no longer create the in-progress label. Repositories relying on automatic creation must explicitly configure that label before requesting in-progress updates.
